title: 06. Typing & Models: PYDANTIC
summary: PYDANTIC: PYDANTIC — Data Validation using Python Type Hints; WHAT: Library for data validation and settings management..

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/pydantic_models.py
# ============================================================
# PYDANTIC — Data Validation using Python Type Hints
# ============================================================
# WHAT: Library for data validation and settings management.
# WHY:  Validates external data (API requests, configs, etc.)
#        with rich error messages and type coercion.

from pydantic import (
    BaseModel, Field, field_validator, model_validator,
    EmailStr, HttpUrl, ConfigDict
)
from typing import Optional
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum

class Role(str, Enum):
    ADMIN = "admin"
    USER = "user"
    MODERATOR = "moderator"

class Address(BaseModel):
    street: str
    city: str
    country: str = "India"
    zip_code: str = Field(..., pattern=r"^\d{6}$")

class User(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(
        str_strip_whitespace=True,  # Strip whitespace from strings
        str_min_length=1,           # No empty strings
        frozen=False,               # Mutable by default
    )
    
    id: int
    name: str = Field(..., min_length=2, max_length=50)
    email: EmailStr
    age: int = Field(ge=18, le=120, description="Must be 18+")
    role: Role = Role.USER
    tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    address: Optional[Address] = None
    created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=datetime.now)
    
    @field_validator("name")
    @classmethod
    def validate_name(cls, v: str) -> str:
        if not v.replace(" ", "").isalpha():
            raise ValueError("Name must contain only letters")
        return v.title()
    
    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_admin_email(self):
        if self.role == Role.ADMIN and not self.email.endswith("@company.com"):
            raise ValueError("Admins must use company email")
        return self

# --- Creating instances ---
user = User(
    id=1,
    name="  veerababu  ",  # Will be stripped and titled
    email="veera@company.com",
    age=30,
    role="admin",           # String coerced to Enum!
    address={"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Hyderabad", "zip_code": "500001"}
)
print(user)
print(user.model_dump())          # Convert to dict
print(user.model_dump_json())     # Convert to JSON string

# --- Validation Errors ---
from pydantic import ValidationError
try:
    User(id=1, name="V", email="bad-email", age=15)
except ValidationError as e:
    print(e.json())  # Detailed error with field, type, message

# --- Pydantic Settings (for config management) ---
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings

class AppSettings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = ConfigDict(env_prefix="APP_")
    
    debug: bool = False
    database_url: str = "sqlite:///default.db"
    secret_key: str
    allowed_hosts: list[str] = ["localhost"]

# Reads from environment: APP_DEBUG, APP_DATABASE_URL, etc.
# settings = AppSettings()  # Reads from env vars

# --- Generic Models ---
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Generic, TypeVar

T = TypeVar("T")

class PaginatedResponse(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    items: list[T]
    total: int
    page: int
    page_size: int
    
    @property
    def total_pages(self) -> int:
        return (self.total + self.page_size - 1) // self.page_size
```

quiz.question: What is Pydantic and why use it?
options: Manages a dynamic number of context managers. Essential when you don't know how many resources you need at write time.
Pydantic: validates and coerces types automatically, generates JSON schema, has rich error reporting.
Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion.
Pydantic validates data using Python type hints. It provides: automatic type coercion, rich validation errors, JSON serialization, and settings management.
quiz.explanation: Pydantic validates data using Python type hints. It provides: automatic type coercion, rich validation errors, JSON serialization, and settings management. Essential for API development with FastAPI.

quiz.question: What is the difference between Pydantic and dataclasses?
options: Manages a dynamic number of context managers. Essential when you don't know how many resources you need at write time.
DEBUG (10) < INFO (20) < WARNING (30) < ERROR (40) < CRITICAL (50).
Factory creates different types of objects through a single interface (which type).
Pydantic: validates and coerces types automatically, generates JSON schema, has rich error reporting.
quiz.explanation: Pydantic: validates and coerces types automatically, generates JSON schema, has rich error reporting. Dataclasses: no validation by default, part of stdlib, lighter weight. Use Pydantic for external data, dataclasses for internal data.

quiz.question: What is Field() used for?
options: Links a new exception to the original cause. raise NewError("msg") from original_error.
Concurrency: dealing with multiple tasks at once (structure).
An iterator is any object with __iter__ and __next__.
Adds constraints and metadata: min_length, max_length, ge, le, pattern, description, default_factory, alias, exclude.
quiz.explanation: Adds constraints and metadata: min_length, max_length, ge, le, pattern, description, default_factory, alias, exclude.

quiz.question: What is the difference between @field_validator and @model_validator?
options: Rotates log files when they reach a size limit. maxBytes sets file size limit, backupCount keeps N backup files.
Percentage of code executed during tests. 80%+ is a common target.
raise (no argument) re-raises the current exception preserving the original traceback. raise e raises e but may alter the traceback.
@field_validator validates a single field. @model_validator validates the entire model (cross-field validation).
quiz.explanation: @field_validator validates a single field. @model_validator validates the entire model (cross-field validation). Model validators can run before (mode="before") or after (mode="after") field validation.

quiz.question: How does Pydantic handle type coercion?
options: When two or more threads wait for each other's locks forever.
yield from sub_gen is equivalent to for item in sub_gen: yield item, but also properly handles send(), throw(), and close().
Read line-by-line (file object is an iterator), use chunk_size for binary files, or use mmap for memory-mapped files.
Pydantic automatically converts compatible types: "123" → 123 (str to int), "admin" → Role.ADMIN (str to enum), "2024-01-01" → datetime object.
quiz.explanation: Pydantic automatically converts compatible types: "123" → 123 (str to int), "admin" → Role.ADMIN (str to enum), "2024-01-01" → datetime object.
